record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: Classical sequential growth models are stochastic causal set dynamics in which a causal set grows element by element, with each new element choosing a random subset of existing elements as causal ancestors under rules preserving causality and a discrete analogue of covariance. Can any such dynamics eventually evolve into a manifoldlike causal set approximating a Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker cosmological universe, and if so by what mechanism?

evidence.quote: A family of these models are known as ‘classical sequential growth’ or CSG models. As the name suggests, in these models, a causal set grows element by element sequentially.

Each new nth element selects a random subset of the existing elements to be in its causal past. While this choice is made randomly or stochastically, there are some rules to ensure that causality and a suitable analog of discrete covariance are preserved by the ancestor selection process.
A major open question is whether and how one of these dynamics eventually evolves into a manifoldlike causal set such as one approximated by a Friedman-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) universe.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A causal set is a locally finite partially ordered set $(C,\preceq)$: a set $C$ equipped with a partial order $\preceq$ (reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive) such that for every $x,z\in C$ the interval $\{y\in C : x\preceq y\preceq z\}$ is finite. A causal set is called manifoldlike if there exists a Lorentzian manifold $(M,g)$ together with a faithful (Poisson) embedding of $C$ into $M$ such that the induced causal order on the image coincides with $\preceq$ and the embedded points are uniformly distributed at unit density with respect to the volume measure of $g$; in this case $(M,g)$ is said to approximate $C$. A Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker (FLRW) spacetime is a Lorentzian manifold of the form $M = I\times \Sigma$ with metric $-dt^2 + a(t)^2\, d\Sigma_k^2$, where $a:I\to(0,\infty)$ is a smooth scale factor and $d\Sigma_k^2$ is a Riemannian metric of constant sectional curvature $k\in\{-1,0,+1\}$ on a $3$-manifold $\Sigma$.

A classical sequential growth (CSG) model is a probabilistic dynamics generating an infinite causal set element by element, indexed by $n=1,2,3,\dots$. At stage $n$ the existing causal set $C_{n-1}$ has $n-1$ elements; a new element $e_n$ is born and assigned a "past" $A\subseteq C_{n-1}$ which must be a downward-closed (ancestral) subset of $C_{n-1}$, with $e_n$ then declared to lie above every element of $A$ and incomparable with every element of $C_{n-1}\setminus A$. The transition probabilities $\mathbb{P}(A\mid C_{n-1})$ must satisfy:
(i) internal temporality: every new element is added to the future or as incomparable, never to the past;
(ii) discrete general covariance: the probability of producing any finite labeled causal poset depends only on its isomorphism class, not on the order in which labels were assigned;
(iii) Bell causality: the relative probability of two ancestor choices that differ only in elements spacelike to all of them is unaffected by adding or removing such spacelike elements.
Let $\mathcal{D}$ denote the family of all such CSG dynamics.

Problem. Does there exist a dynamics in $\mathcal{D}$ whose almost-sure (or typical, in an appropriate probabilistic sense) limiting causal set is manifoldlike and is approximated by some FLRW spacetime $(I\times\Sigma, -dt^2 + a(t)^2\,d\Sigma_k^2)$? If so, exhibit the dynamics and identify the mechanism by which the FLRW geometry, including its scale factor $a(t)$ and spatial curvature $k$, emerges from the stochastic growth rules.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether classical sequential growth dynamics for causal sets can produce a manifoldlike causal set approximated by an FLRW spacetime is widely regarded as a major open problem in causal set theory. Partial results indicate de Sitter-like exponential expansion near "origin" elements, and recent path-integral work shows that non-manifoldlike causal sets are strongly suppressed; however, no CSG dynamics is known to almost-surely produce an FLRW-approximating causal set, and the mechanism remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The emergence of spacetime from causal sets (Chapter 3)
status_evidence.snippet: Manifoldlike causal sets appear to be a vanishingly small subset; producing them dynamically remains a central problem.
status_evidence.claim: Recovering manifoldlike (and thus FLRW-like) causal sets from dynamics is an open challenge.

status_evidence.title: Indications of de Sitter spacetime from classical sequential growth dynamics of causal sets
status_evidence.snippet: Effective dynamics near origin elements suggests an initial period of de Sitter-like exponential expansion.
status_evidence.claim: There is partial evidence of cosmological (de Sitter / FLRW-like) behavior in CSG models, but full emergence is not established.

status_evidence.title: Causal sets and an emerging continuum
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results show that almost all non-manifoldlike causal sets are strongly suppressed in the gravitational path integral.
status_evidence.claim: Progress has been made on suppressing non-manifoldlike sets, but FLRW emergence from CSG is not demonstrated.
